$comment: The single source of truth for the analysis toolchain (design review §D3).
THREE CONSUMERS, ONE FILE:
1. `apps/server/sandbox-base.Dockerfile` reads these as build ARGs (WP2).
That is also what fixes the two installs that float today: semgrep via
`pipx install semgrep` and uv via `astral.sh/uv/install.sh`.
2. `packages/code-facts` probes each binary at run time and STAMPS what it
actually resolved into the facts envelope (`toolchain` beside `coverage`
and `degraded[]`), so every scorecard records which toolchain produced
it.
3. The eval preflight compares each `--version` against this manifest and
refuses on a mismatch, printing the commands to fix it. It never
installs silently.
The failure this closes is SILENT VERSION DRIFT: measure a rung on host
Opengrep 1.27, ship an image with 1.0, and production generates a different
obligation set from the one every gate was read on. Nothing would error.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY *NOT* HERE: the npm-resolved engines (ts-morph,
@ast-grep/napi, zod). They are pinned by `package.json` + `pnpm-lock.yaml`,
which is a stronger pin than a hand-maintained copy, and duplicating them
here would create exactly the drift this file exists to prevent. The
envelope stamps their RESOLVED versions instead, read off the installed
package.json at run time — see `src/toolchain.ts`.
BUMPING A VERSION invalidates comparability with every measurement taken
before it. Record the bump in the eval run notes.

opengrep.note: The engine slot for the review path — NOT Semgrep, whose registry rules moved to a licence that plausibly excludes a review product (locked decision 7). Not installable from npm: the `opengrep` npm name is a 145-byte empty stub held by Aikido.

gitleaks.note: Already pinned at exactly this version in sandbox-base.Dockerfile — recorded here so WP2's change is a refactor, not a bump. The `gitleaks` npm name is an unrelated third-party package.

ast-grep.note: The CLI, for interactive use inside the sandbox. `code-facts` itself uses the in-process @ast-grep/napi binding at the SAME version, so keep the two in step when bumping either.

semgrep.note: FLOATS today (`pipx install semgrep`). Belongs to the separate `security-review` workflow, which this plan does not touch — pinned here only so the image stops drifting (§D3/§E4).

uv.note: FLOATS today. Runs `type: script` (runtime: python) phases; pinned here for the same reason as semgrep.
